candidates.exact_span: There shall be no discharge of floating solids or visible foam in other than trace amounts.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a qualitative enforceable limit rather than a numeric one; whether a reported measurement is subject to numeric exceedance comparison versus a different compliance evaluation depends on how 'trace amounts' and 'no discharge' are interpreted.

candidates.exact_span: There shall be no discharge of visible films of oil, globules of oil, grease or solids in or on the water, or coatings on stream banks.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines additional qualitative effluent limitations; interpretation of what constitutes a prohibited visible film, globule, or coating could change which limit is deemed applicable and whether numeric limit comparison is appropriate.

candidates.exact_span: Samples taken in compliance with the monitoring requirements specified above shall be taken at the discharge from the final treatment unit prior to the receiving stream.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies the required sampling location for compliance-related samples; a different reading of 'final treatment unit' or 'discharge' could change which reported measurements are tied to applicable limits (A) and whether monitoring was performed at the required point (B).

candidates.exact_span: Achieve Final Effluent Limitations 12 months after permit effective date
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets when Cyanide effluent limitations become enforceable; the computed permit effective date and whether a given FY2025 monitoring period falls before or after that date changes which limits apply (A) and when related monitoring/compliance obligations attach (B).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall submit a progress report to both EPA and NMED outlining the status of the activities (i.e., analyzers installation, Process Optimization Study, etc.) during the months of January, April, July, and October, of each year, until compliance is achieved as stated above.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates recurring reporting obligations tied to the cyanide compliance schedule; interpretation of 'until compliance is achieved' and which months in FY2025 trigger the requirement could change whether monitoring/reporting was required for a given period.

candidates.exact_span: No later than 14 calendar days following the date for compliance for Cyanide effluent limitations, the permittee shall submit a written notice of compliance or noncompliance.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes a one-time reporting obligation keyed to the cyanide compliance deadline; the computed compliance date determines whether this notice was required during FY2025 and whether absence of evidence reflects non-applicability versus missing required documentation.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall achieve compliance with the TDS net increase effluent concentration limit of 449 mg/L 3 years after the permit effective date.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States an enforceable numeric TDS limit and a delayed effective date; interpretation of 'net increase effluent concentration' and the three-year schedule determines whether 449 mg/L is the applicable limit for FY2025 measurements and monitoring periods.

candidates.exact_span: 2. Complete constructions and cease discharging                 November 2024
candidates.computation_change_reason: Schedules cessation of WTP #1 discharge to the WWTP; whether and when that discharge ceased affects which effluent limits and monitoring points apply (A), whether discharge-dependent monitoring was required after November 2024 (B), and whether missing results reflect a documented no-discharge period versus inadequate evidence (C).
